metadata.note: Step 5 separates penalty expectation from open play, shrinks team penalty rates toward the league, scales them by fixture attack strength, uses explicit taker shares, and applies data-derived role assist calibration. Remaining INTERIM values retain their original upgrade dates.

status_legend.INTERIM: neutral starting value, not a measured result; upgrade_date names when the fitted value lands
status_legend.DERIVED: computed at runtime from the loaded archive, never stored as a constant
status_legend.CALIBRATED: fitted by the calibration harness and frozen against a model version

tuning._left_at_default: Every other setting was tested and left alone, because changing it did not improve the gameweeks the search could not see.

rho._proved_by: Measured by walking each engine setting on 2025-26 gameweeks 10 to 28, then kept only because it also improved gameweeks 29 to 38, which the search never saw: ordering 0.4238 to 0.4465, error 1.773 to 1.755, top-twenty hits 3.30 to 3.50 of 20, surviving 100% of 150 redraws of the season. 2026-27 keeps defensive contribution, so the values tuned under those rules are the ones that apply here.

grid_cap.note: truncation error measured and recorded by the calibration run

finishing_k.note: shot count at which finishing evidence carries half weight

finishing_clamp.note: bound on the finishing multiplier; the calibrated bound comes out of the backtest

pen_attempt_k.note: attempts at which a taker's own conversion carries half weight against the league rate

penalty_spot_xg.note: Used only to recover historical penalty-event volume from the difference between xG and non-penalty xG when the archive has no penalty-attempt counts.

positional_share_priors.note: computed from the loaded squads at run time (layer2.positionalSharePriors)

role_rate_priors.note: Broad football roles and their npxG/xA rates are derived on every run from the full prior-season history table. They are used as hierarchical shrinkage targets; no player receives a manual star boost.

penalty_award_rate.note: Team attempts per match are shrunk toward the league rate, then adjusted by fixture attacking lambda. A zero-penalty prior season no longer means zero future penalty expectation.

penalty_conversion.note: league conversion from the archive, shrunk toward the taker's own record

promoted_decay_to_gw.note: 01 §3.9 names GW10 as the decay endpoint; the cohort prior itself is fitted at B-25

promoted_prior.note: position-conditioned share prior fitted on the last five promoted cohorts (B-25). Null until fitted: while null, promoted players are shrunk by k_pos only and carry the LOW SAMPLE marker

pen_rate_shrink_matches.note: One season of league-rate exposure prevents a club with zero or unusually many penalties last year from being treated as a certainty. Refit by walk-forward penalty-event likelihood.

pen_lambda_exponent.note: Fixture penalty expectation scales with the square root of team lambda relative to the league team-goal mean. This moves less aggressively than goals while recognising that strong attacking fixtures produce more box entries and penalties.

pen_lambda_min_scale.note: Lower safety bound on fixture penalty-rate scaling.

pen_lambda_max_scale.note: Upper safety bound on fixture penalty-rate scaling.

penalty_taker_share.note: One explicit rank-one taker receives the full share. Multiple ranked takers split the role using stored confidence and evidence; historical attempts are used only where no current hierarchy exists.

role_assist_calibration.note: Role-level actual-assist share divided by role-level xA share, derived from the prior-season population and applied only where the role sample is substantial.

k_survive.note: Shrinkage of survive-past-60 rate. Fitted the same way; the optimum is a true interior one, tested to 512. Brier 0.04175 against 0.04305 at the previous 4. Heavy shrinkage is correct here: an individual's survive-60 rate barely predicts, so almost everyone should sit near the league mean.

p_start_ceiling.note: Observed maximum season start rate is exactly 1.0: players do start every match. The previous 0.97 cap was arbitrary and clipped genuinely nailed starters.

early_sub_share.note: Share of cameos entering early enough to reach 60 minutes. Measured directly over 17,121 cameos across nine seasons. The previous 0.12 understated it by 43 per cent.

wc_prior.note: World Cup load penalty applied GW1-4. Null until the fatigue study delivers; while null NO fatigue effect is applied at all — the model does not guess

newcomer_start_rate.note: Start rate of players with NO previous PL season, derived 2026-07-29 from two cohorts of the public archive: 2025-26 newcomers started 19.4% of matches (361 players), 2024-25 newcomers 16.3%. Used as the base start chance for a player with no record, replacing the league-wide rate (~0.5 among regulars) which had new signings outranking established starters in the lineup sampler. Team news and real minutes override it within days.

n_sims.note: 01 §3.4 specifies N=10,000. Measured on a realistic load (3 gameweeks, 10 fixtures each, 22 players per side): 37s and 20MB, well inside the Actions window, so the spec value ships. N is stamped on every model_versions row

seed.note: fixed so every run is reproducible bit for bit

full_time.note: goal-minute draw horizon; switches to the empirical archive minute distribution if late-goal skew is material

xp_visible.note: Opened 29 Jul 2026. The fallback scorer was measured against the whole of 2025/26 with jobs/backtest.mjs: it beat a naive per-player average by 3 per cent, and a sweep across five settings for its main parameter moved rank accuracy by 0.002. The limit is the fallback's structure, not its tuning. It scales one blended season average and cannot separate a defender who scores from one who keeps clean sheets. The engine prices goals, assists, clean sheets, saves and the bonus race separately, which is the structure the fallback lacks, so it is the better bet even before it is validated. It CANNOT be validated yet because it projects matches not yet played. Re-measure once GW1 is done and close this again if it fails to beat 3 per cent.

league_rates._what: League per-90 xG and xA by position, minutes-weighted, derived from the full 2025-26 archive by deriveLeagueRates on 2026-07-29. Used to price a player with no Premier League history at his position's average threat instead of zero, which was concentrating promoted clubs' entire attack onto their two or three players with any record (Diop projected 9.3, top of the league, GW1 preview). The live run re-derives from the current season once ten full matches exist and this fallback stops being used. Extended 2026-07-29 with clearance/block/interception and recovery rates per 90 by position, used to shrink thin-sample defensive rates toward the league norm (a 7-start hot streak was being trusted like a full season and putting squad players in the GW1 top ten).
